useCase.actions: Read users' emails and draft replies

summary.routeReason: Composio lists Gmail among toolkits with Composio-managed OAuth, so a prototype can skip Google Cloud setup. A branded external product needs its own Google OAuth client: the managed app shows Composio's name on consent and shares Composio's quota, and your own verification and security assessment cover your app, not theirs.
summary.difficultyReason: Both scopes this use case needs (gmail.readonly, gmail.compose) are restricted. Going to production means brand verification, restricted scope verification, a permitted-use-case check, and an annual third-party CASA security assessment if data touches your servers.

testingBeforeReview.text: Yes, in Testing status with up to 100 test users you list. Testers see a warning screen, and with External user type their refresh tokens expire in 7 days.

mainBlocker.text: Restricted scope verification plus a security assessment from a Google-empanelled assessor, repeated at least every 12 months, for apps that access restricted data from or through a server.

summary.nextAction: Create the Google Cloud project, set branding on a domain you own, add gmail.readonly and gmail.compose, add test users, and start brand verification early.

managedOAuth.text: Composio provides a managed OAuth app for Gmail, so you can prototype without registering one. Users then see Composio's name on the consent screen and share its rate-limit quota, so an external launch usually brings its own app.

activeWork.text: Hours for project, consent screen and client setup; days to prepare privacy policy, scope justifications and demo video; assessment prep depends on your stack. Our estimate.

reviewWait.text: Google states: brand verification typically a few minutes automated, manual review usually 2-3 business days; restricted scope verification 'can potentially take several weeks'. No fixed end date is published for restricted review or CASA.

policyDeadlines.text: Security assessment must be redone at least every 12 months after the assessor's Letter of Assessment approval date to keep restricted scopes.
Unverified apps showing the unverified app screen are limited to 100 new users in total.

costs.text: The security assessment is done by an independent, Google-approved third party. Google pages we fetched do not state the fee; secondary sources say the developer pays the assessor.

prerequisites.text: A domain you own, verified in Google Search Console, covering your homepage, privacy policy and terms URLs.
A public homepage and a privacy policy on the same domain that explains how you access, use, store and share Google user data.
Your use case must be a permitted Gmail app type, e.g. one that enhances the email experience for productivity. No training general AI models on user data.

permissions.reviewImpact: Restricted: restricted scope verification plus security assessment if accessed via your server.

permissions.enables: Manage drafts and send emails (needed to create draft replies).
permissions.reviewImpact: Restricted, same as above. Note it also allows sending.

permissions.enables: Send email on the user's behalf only; cannot read or draft.
permissions.reviewImpact: Sensitive: sensitive scope verification (up to 10 days per Google), no security assessment.

steps.title: Create a Google Cloud project and enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: Use an organization-owned project if possible.

steps.title: Set branding and External audience
steps.detail: App name, logo, support email, homepage, privacy policy, terms, authorized domains. User type External.
steps.outcome: Consent screen configured in Testing status.

steps.title: Declare scopes and create the OAuth client
steps.detail: Data access: add gmail.readonly and gmail.compose only. Clients: create a Web client with your redirect URIs.

steps.title: Add test users and test the flow
steps.detail: Up to 100 test users; each one uses quota once added. Expect re-consent every 7 days because testing refresh tokens expire.
steps.outcome: Read inbox and create a draft for a test user.

steps.title: Verify domain and pass brand verification
steps.detail: Verify domains in Search Console, then Verify Branding. Required before data access verification.

steps.title: Submit restricted scope verification
steps.detail: In the Verification Center: justification per scope, why narrower scopes won't work, unlisted YouTube demo video of the consent flow, permitted app type.
steps.outcome: Google review of data access starts.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment
steps.detail: Required because the agent reads mail on your servers. Done by a Google-empanelled assessor under the App Defense Alliance CASA framework.
steps.outcome: Letter of Assessment sent to Google.

steps.title: Publish to production
steps.detail: Switch publishing status to In production once verified; any Google user can then authorize without the unverified screen.
steps.outcome: No 100-user cap, no 7-day token expiry from Testing status.

steps.title: Annual reassessment
steps.detail: Reverify and redo the security assessment at least every 12 months; adding a new restricted scope may need reassessment.

steps.title: Keep to Limited Use rules
steps.detail: Use data only for the user-facing feature; no humans reading mail without explicit consent; no training general models.

blockers.symptom: Test users must re-connect every week.
blockers.cause: External apps in Testing status get refresh tokens that expire in 7 days (unless only basic profile scopes are used).
blockers.nextAction: Expected in testing; it ends only after moving to production.

blockers.symptom: Users see 'Google hasn't verified this app' and sign-ups stop at 100.
blockers.cause: Unverified app screen and 100-new-user cap for unverified apps.
blockers.nextAction: Finish brand and restricted scope verification.

blockers.symptom: Verification rejected or stalled on use case.
blockers.cause: App type not in Gmail's permitted list, or scopes broader than the feature needs.
blockers.nextAction: Frame the agent as productivity enhancement, request only readonly + compose, and show it in the demo video.

blockers.cause: Domains not verified in Search Console, homepage behind login, or privacy policy on another domain.
blockers.nextAction: Fix domain ownership and host the policy on the homepage domain.

blockers.symptom: Gmail access stops after a user changes password.
blockers.cause: Refresh tokens with Gmail scopes are revoked on password change.

agentCan: Fill redirect URIs, scopes and consent screen text
Draft scope justifications and explain why gmail.send or metadata won't do
Draft the privacy policy against Google's disclosure checklist
Write the demo video script and prepare the CASA self-scan inputs
humanMust: Log in to Google Cloud and own the project
Verify the domain in Search Console
Record and upload the demo video
Choose and pay the security assessor, and answer their questions

sources.title: Choose Gmail API scopes
sources.note: gmail.readonly Restricted; gmail.compose Restricted ("Manage drafts and send emails"); gmail.send Sensitive.

sources.title: Restricted scope verification
sources.note: "can potentially take several weeks"; assessment "at least every 12 months"; required for data "from or through a third-party server".

sources.title: Sensitive scope verification
sources.note: "can take up to 10 days to complete"; justification per scope and demo video required.

sources.title: Brand verification
sources.note: Verify domains in Search Console; manual review "usually takes 2-3 business days".

sources.title: Using OAuth 2.0 to Access Google APIs
sources.note: External + Testing "is issued a refresh token expiring in 7 days"; password change revokes Gmail-scope tokens.

sources.title: Manage app audience (Google Cloud Help)
sources.note: Testing "limited to up to 100 test users"; a test user "consumes a project's test user quota once added".

sources.title: Unverified apps (Google Cloud Help)
sources.note: "limited to 100 new users until it is verified"; verification "might require several months".

sources.title: Gmail API policy
sources.note: Permitted: "Applications that enhance the email experience for productivity purposes"; no AI model training on user data.

sources.title: App Defense Alliance: CASA
sources.note: CASA uses a "risk-based, multi-tier assessment approach". Page we read gives no fees or durations.

sources.title: Composio: managed vs custom auth
sources.note: Managed: "Users see Composio's app name during OAuth." "Managed apps share quota across all Composio users."

sources.title: Unauthenticated request to Google Auth Platform pages

attempts.intended: Open the Google Auth Platform client and audience pages.
attempts.result: Both returned HTTP 302 Found to https://accounts.google.com/ServiceLogin?service=cloudconsole&...&continue=<the page>.
attempts.stoppedAt: Google sign-in. We did not log in, create a project or submit anything.
attempts.proves: These Google Auth Platform URLs exist and need a signed-in Google account.
attempts.doesNotProve: Current console fields, whether verification is required for our exact scopes in practice, or real review time.
attempts.correction: Google now splits the old 'OAuth consent screen' into Branding, Audience, Data access and Clients pages under /auth; older guides point to APIs & Services > OAuth consent screen.

uncertainties: CASA fee and tier: not stated on the Google or App Defense Alliance pages we fetched; secondary blogs give varying figures, so we quote none.

Total time to production for restricted scopes is not published as a fixed number; Google says 'several weeks' for restricted verification and elsewhere 'several months' for verification depending on data sensitivity.
Whether Composio's managed Gmail app is fully verified for restricted scopes was not checked.
conflicts: Google gives different time language on different pages: 'several weeks' (restricted scope page) vs 'might require several months' (unverified apps help page). We show both and do not pick a single number.
